questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew that Barcelona is a city with lots of international students, which would be a great opportunity to meet people from around the world. I also knew that the city had a lot to offer as far as culture and beautiful architecture. Furthermore, the University of Barcelona had a good program for Urban Economics which is a subject i find very interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The assistance upon arrival was good. I was invited to a welcome session at the University and was provided help with my enrollment at their international relations office.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A welcome session that introduced me to university and what i needed to know regarding courses etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found a room through someone i knew, but i also moved while i was there where i used the site Idealista to find the new room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Lots of areas are good but perhaps stay away from El Raval.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The accomodations options that the university offered where very pricy.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just had to go to the international relations office and was helped with the enrollment. I had to provide a photo and my passport and then they registered me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had a service desk and and international office which helped a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. They were flexible and i was able to switch courses within the first one or two weeks.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They can be a bit slow to answer on email, but you can usually just call them and then they can answer your questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course were okay, but it is not like normal university lectures. It is small classes with a lot of interactions, which you have to get used to. I would advice against choosing the course Industrial Organization and Regulation due to unusual method of evaluation. They offer continuous evaluation while still requiring one to pass the final exam even thought the average grade is enough to pass. Furthermore the workload is out of proportion relative to all of the other courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were acceptable except for the course Industrial Organization and Regulation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. It felt more like Gymnasium. The classes were small and we had to do a lot of presentations

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Spatial Econometrics
Economic Geography
Industrial Organization and Regulation
Economic Growth I
Market Design and Experiments
Empirical Methods in Regional and Urban Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic Geography - Very good teachers

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: One of my appartments had bed bugs so i had to move. I lost about 17000dkk in lost deposits and rents

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent and food was more expensive than i expected. Public transport was much cheaper than i expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had padel training at a very low price. That was nice

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a sports club with tennis and padel tennis

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Padel training was really nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go a roadtrip, go to morocco, go to Primavera Festival, go hiking on Montserrat.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. They speak a bit of english

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The erasmus events are good as far as i know. One thing to note is that the Master starts before the bachelor, so many of the other exchange students are not arriving before one month later.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really that much. You eat abit later

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The slow-life. Sitting at a cafe and getting a coffee for cheap prices.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The master begins before the bachelor, so it can be a bit lonely at the start, but UCPH had a facebook page where you could find other danish students in Barcelona

The evaluation is usually based on continuous assesment which means that there is a lot to hand in during the semester. It would be nice to be prepared for this.

Do not choose the course Industrial Organization and Regulation

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends that i made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being alone in the start

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
